messages:
Alex: FYI pushed PR #8372 (kv-prefetch tweak) to canary this morning and the canary run is showing a regression on longseq workloads. p95 jumped. Need quick eyes, attaching artifacts. :eyes:
Priya: link to artifacts? can you paste the bench command you used?
Alex: sure — ran the nightly microbench harness: `./bench/run_longseq.sh --model=redwood-4k --iter=200 --batch=4` results uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/bench/4444202468/ and grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/longseq-canary?orgId=1
Sam: saw the s3 artifacts. p95 baseline ~48ms, canary ~122ms at 4k seq, mem per worker +340MB. throughput (tokens/s) down ~12%.
Megan: ugh. Any diffs in kernel selection or quant path?
Alex: diff in runtime: change in prefetch heuristic + a small scheduling tweak in allocator. No kernel changes. See diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8372/files
Jin: @Alex can you include flamegraphs? I want to see if it's KV cache miss behavior or scheduler stalls.
Alex: flamegraphs attached in the artifact bucket (flame-*.html). Early look shows increased time in `apply_prefetch()` and a spike in `worker_wait()` stacks.
build-bot: Canary deployment 8372 -> canary-4 completed at 2026-03-15T09:14:02Z. 40/40 health checks passed.
Priya: good. Do we have a quick repro to run locally to bisect the heuristic change?
Alex: yep — checkout branch `pr/8372-regheur` and run `./scripts/repro_longseq --seq 4096 --iters 50 --seed 13` should reproduce locally on a machine with >=48GB GPU RAM.
Sam: I'll run the repro in CI job `ci/bench-longseq-quick` and post results. If it reproduces, we should revert the prefetch part and keep the allocator tweak separate.
Megan: @Priya can you weigh in on rollback risk? allocator tweak was to reduce fragmentation, still want that.
Priya: if revert prefetch only, allocator stays. Low churn. I'm +1 to revert prefetch until we fix the edge-case. Need one more sign-off from infra.
Jin: I'll follow up with microbench flamegraphs, but preliminary claim: prefetch causes more contention on kv-shard locks at high seq lengths.
Alex: thanks. tagging @Sam @Megan for a quick review on the revert PR I opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8385 — revert prefetch heuristics and add a test that exercises high-seq layouts.
Sam: running CI now. If CI + quick bench look good I'll approve.
Megan: :thumbsup: please hold merge until we have one more infra approval and CI passes. Alex, can you add a short note in the PR description summarizing the perf delta numbers?
Alex: will do, added numbers and links to artifacts. Holding merge until 2nd infra + CI green.
Priya: thanks, team. If Sam or Jin find nothing else, we can reintroduce a safer prefetch variant behind a flag and gate with canary.
Alex: plan noted. I'll post updates here with CI/bench results.
Sam: CI finished: quick bench repro shows p95 back to 49ms after revert. posting logs to s3://redwood-ci/bench/4444202468/revert-check.txt
Alex: great, thanks. I'll request merge once infra sign-off comes in.
Jin: gave infra review +1. looks fine.
Megan: giving final ack once PR description has the mitigation plan.
Alex: added mitigation + follow-up TODOs. requesting merge window for next 30min.
Megan: merging now, please monitor canary dashboards for next 2 hours and file a follow-up if anything pops. :rocket:
